content.text: I can see this is a Next.js 16 app using the App Router. To log every request to the console, I'll create a middleware file that will intercept all requests. This is the recommended approach in Next.js for request logging.

Perfect! I've added request logging to your Next.js app by creating a middleware file at `/vercel/sandbox/middleware.ts`.

This middleware will:
- Log every incoming request with a timestamp, HTTP method, and full URL
- Include the User-Agent header to identify the client
- Include the IP address (from x-forwarded-for or x-real-ip headers)
- Automatically apply to all routes except Next.js internal routes (_next/static, _next/image, favicon.ico)

When you run your app with `npm run dev` or `npm start`, you'll see console output like:

```
[2026-02-18T10:30:45.123Z] GET http://localhost:3000/
  User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0...
  IP: 127.0.0.1
```

The logs will appear in your terminal where the Next.js server is running.
